key_insight: The paper proposes a smooth, closed-form elastoplastic-damage update for graphics simulation that preserves irreversible history without local Newton solves.
engineering_relevance: It offers a compact, vectorizable material model for explicit solid simulation when smooth branch activation and simple implementation matter more than exact yield-surface enforcement.
method: Softplus generates a candidate plastic strain, then a max-history projection enforces irreversibility.
A deviatoric plastic-strain tensor stores residual direction while an exponential damage variable evolves from the saved history.
Active and frozen branches are evaluated analytically from one response energy, avoiding local iterative solves.
evidence_signal: The method was validated on cyclic tension, cantilever bending, platen compression, and a torus, showing residual deformation, monotone internal variables, and branchwise energy-gradient agreement, with proportional-loading error of 1.53% but 49.39% under a 90-degree path turn.
watch_item: It is intended for isotropic, proportional or near-proportional loading and is not a substitute for general return mapping, anisotropic damage, or phase-field fracture.
paper_title: A Smooth Explicit Elastoplastic--Damage Update for Graphics Simulation
